$comment: Plugin scope policy — which agent contexts each protocol injector may inject into. Sole consumer: plugins/shared/plugin-scope.ts (opencode has no native plugin-to-agent scoping). Permission/tools policy does NOT live here — those are native opencode fields in opencode.template.jsonc. Keys starting with $ are documentation, ignored by the consumer.
$semantics: plugins.<id> holds the policy for one injector; '*' is the default inherited by every plugin without its own entry. Each policy: deny = blacklist of scope entries, allow = whitelist (if present, ONLY listed entries pass); on conflict deny wins. Scope entry grammar: 'x' matches identity or state x; 'x:*' matches state x (any identity); 'x:y' matches state x with identity y (reserved — identity-in-state detection is not wired yet). No match and no detected context = allowed (fail-open).
$identifiers: Text detection rules for contexts opencode cannot name (system.transform carries no agent identifier): 'contains' — any system entry contains the string; 'startsWith' — the first system entry starts with it. Keys are scope names used in deny/allow values. The subagent state needs no rule: plugin-scope.ts detects it via session parentID.

*.$comment: lite strips its own overhead; utility (title generation, ~30k tok saved per session) and every subagent step are narrow specialists — orchestration protocol text is pure waste there.

project-profiler.$comment: Backend routing is a subagent's work discipline AND a Lite concern (Lite now defaults to tgrep_search per prompts/lite.md). Utility (title-generator, ~30k tok saved per session) stays out — it never touches code search, so the block is pure overhead there.

project-memory.$comment: Curated project lessons are the agent's working discipline — Lite sessions need them most (they carry no other project context). Only utility (title generation) and subagent steps stay denied.

project-memory-note-tool.$comment: Tool gate for memory_note — same policy engine as system-inject, different plugin ID so the two gates stay independently tunable. Utility sessions (title generator) deny: title tasks are too narrow to discover reusable rules, and a stray note pollutes public.md / private.md with noise. Subagent ALLOWed: subagents may genuinely learn a project quirk worth remembering (e.g. advisor subagent fixes a bug and discovers 'this repo's CI needs --no-sandbox on Windows').
